doc.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021

title: New York gig scene then and now
summary: Weiss moved to New York at the end of 1981; there were many more gigs and jazz restaurants in the 80s and 90s, and live music of all kinds has declined since.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: This is a broad question. You moved to New York in the 80s, is that correct?
Well the very end of 1981. By January of 1982 I had an apartment and I was in. So I’m about reaching my fortieth anniversary as a New Yorker.
If we can ignore the Covid time for a moment, can you compare the way you made a living back then, in the 80s, and what you’re doing now? And does it reflect New York as a jazz scene?

There were a lot more gigs, to put it simply. There were a lot more gigs to be had for piano players in New York in the 80s and the 90s, because I guess — well there were a lot of clubs but there were also restaurants that had jazz and had very good jazz pianists and had good pianos. And I don’t know, there seemed to be a lot more to do, overall.
Well just fewer clubs, fewer restaurants having jazz. I don’t know the reason.

Is jazz a hard sell these days more than it used to be? It’s never — it’s been a long time since it was sort of the popular music of the day, but I wonder as time goes by if people’s attention span and their listening habits make it harder to sort of sell jazz.

I think it’s live music of all kinds have been affected across the board, from the top down. From the most popular pop stars, you know, down to the semi-professional, or semi- amateur solo folk guitarist. I think it’s — live music has been affected across the board. And I don’t know if it just has to do with advances in technology, the internet, but I mean I think of in the 80s even Madison Square Garden, Giants Stadium, pop stars would fill — you know Billy Joel to Bruce Springsteen, Madonna, Prince, Michael Jackson,
whoever, would fill 50,000 seat stadiums regularly. And I don’t think that exists for them anymore either.
